subject: [PATCH v3 0/2] memcg: reduce cacheline contention from lruvec stat

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that even though the patch rearranges struct mem_cgroup_per_node to pair its read-mostly line with a cold line, it does not guarantee that every read-mostly line will be paired with a cold line due to SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN slab usage, which can align objects to 128-byte boundaries but still allow adjacent objects to share a cacheline pair.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks.  A local AI review pointed out a thing:

  One limitation worth mentioning in the [1/2] changelog: the slab
  uses SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN, which need not align each object to a
  128-byte boundary.  If an object starts 64 bytes into such a pair,
  its first line can still be paired with the end of the preceding
  object rather than its own cold line.  This isn't a correctness
  issue, and the measured Skylake improvement may well be real, but the
  layout doesn't guarantee that every read-mostly line pairs with a
  cold line.

2026-10-23.patch_summary: This patch reduces cacheline contention between lruvec stat updates and LRU lists by rearranging the layout of struct mem_cgroup_per_node to pair read-mostly lines with cold lines, and modifying folio and kmem stat updates to avoid going through the lruvec. This change improves performance on systems that use spatial prefetching, such as Intel CPUs. The patch includes two changes: one that reorders the fields in struct mem_cgroup_per_node, and another that modifies the stat update functions to skip using the lruvec. The results show a significant improvement in pages per second for threads faulting in and freeing memory in a single memcg.
